document.title: docs(adr): host control sliced delivery and topology
document.summary: ADR 0004 records how Host Control lands as three PRs, recommends a link-once topology where the Vita calls the companion, and keeps one HTTP parser; `CONTEXT.md` gains three glossary terms that the ADR uses.
document.why: Draft PR #16 grew too large to rebase, and [vendoring a second HTTP parser alongside the hand-rolled upload server needs an ADR](source:s1) before the native slice starts.

sources.title: Decide the fate of draft PR #16 (host control) and re-slice the work
sources.gist: Close #16, land host control as contract, companion, and native-link PRs, and write an ADR on the second HTTP parser.

lookFor: [#45](source:s1) asks to close #5 in favour of #45; this PR does not close #5, and #45 stays open until Máté confirms the recommendations.

[#45](source:s1) asks to fold the useful #16 design docs into the ADR; the ADR summarises their conclusions in prose instead of copying their tables, so details like port defaults and the long-poll variant live only on the closed branch.
The topology section is a recommendation pending confirmation, not a settled decision; the ADR says to rewrite it together with the HTTP parsing section if option B wins.

groups.title: ADR 0004: slices, topology, parser, deferrals
groups.why: [#45](source:s1) requires an ADR before the native slice and asks for the work to be re-sliced into three PRs.
groups.summary: The ADR's topology choice (Vita calls the companion over existing `fetch()`) is what lets its parser section reject picohttpparser and its delivery section keep slice (c) small.
lookFor: Subtle: the ADR claims `header_value` in `src/upload/http_server.c` matches header names case-sensitively and that Node's `fetch` sends `content-length`; a Node `fetch` POST to the upload server today would therefore get a 400 for a missing Content-Length.
The link listener is Shell-gated and stops after a successful link, which reverses #16's always-on shared LAN listener; the Runtime Upload lifecycle stays as `CONTEXT.md` describes it.
The ADR makes a credential decision a prerequisite for the first command that acts on the computer, because the companion accepts commands from any LAN peer in v1.

groups.title: Glossary: Host Control, Host Companion, Host Control Link
groups.why: The ADR names three user-visible concepts that `CONTEXT.md` does not define yet.
groups.summary: The new Language entries define the three terms, and the new Relationships bullets tie them to the existing Runtime Upload and Upload Pairing terms without changing those entries.
lookFor: **Host Companion** reuses the word "host", which `AGENTS.md` uses for the desktop build of VitaDeck; the entry disambiguates in its definition and lists "host build" under _Avoid_.

commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Record ADR 0004: deliver Host Control as contract, companion, and native
link PRs; recommend link-once with Vita-to-companion commands; keep one
HTTP parser. Add Host Control, Host Companion, and Host Control Link to
the glossary.
